concepts.definition: Looks at the voltage on a pin set as an input and returns HIGH (about 5 V) or LOW (about 0 V).
concepts.example: The command int durum = digitalRead(2); puts the current value of D2 into the durum variable.
concepts.pitfall: Reading the pin without making it an input in setup(), or calling it without using the result.

concepts.definition: Makes the pin an input, switches on the resistor inside the board and pulls the pin towards 5 V; no outside resistor is needed.
concepts.example: You write pinMode(2, INPUT_PULLUP); and connect one end of the button to D2 and the other to GND.
concepts.pitfall: Writing only INPUT: the pin floats and the reading is random.

concepts.definition: An input pin not connected to any voltage; it picks up noise from its surroundings and reads unreliably.
concepts.example: You connected the button to D2 but there is no pull-up; while the button is open, digitalRead gives HIGH one moment and LOW the next.
concepts.pitfall: Thinking the random reading is a bug in the code; the problem is usually in the circuit.

concepts.definition: With INPUT_PULLUP the button is connected to GND, so it reads LOW when pressed and HIGH when not pressed.
concepts.example: When not pressed, digitalRead(2) is HIGH; to make the LED light with the button you write 1 - durum.
concepts.pitfall: Expecting HIGH when pressed; the program works the opposite way.

concepts.definition: The voltage limit that decides whether the pin counts as HIGH or LOW. In the lab it is 2.5 V.
concepts.example: If the pin is at 4.9 V it reads HIGH; at 0.1 V it reads LOW.
concepts.pitfall: Thinking a digital input also measures in-between values; digitalRead gives only two results.

quiz.prompt: One end of the button is connected to D2, the other to GND, and the code says pinMode(2, INPUT_PULLUP);. What does digitalRead(2) return while the button is NOT pressed?
quiz.explanation: The internal pull-up resistor pulls the pin to 5 V; while the button is open the pin is not connected to anything else, so it reads HIGH. LOW only comes when the button connects the pin to GND. Random readings happen on a floating input without a pull-up.

When not pressed, d = HIGH = 1. D13 gets 1 (it lights) and D12 gets 1 - 1 = 0 (it goes off). When you press the button, d = 0 and it flips: D12 lights and D13 goes off. The two LEDs are never lit together, because one gets d and the other gets the opposite of d.

pinMode(2, INPUT) does not switch on the pull-up; while the button is open, D2 becomes a floating input and reads at random. It should say INPUT_PULLUP. The expression 1 - digitalRead(2) is not wrong; it only flips the value.

quiz.prompt: In the lab model the internal pull-up resistor is 35 kΩ. The button is pressed and the pin is connected to GND (ignore the button's resistance). How many mA flow from 5 V through this resistor to GND? (Give up to three decimal places.)
quiz.explanation: Ohm's law: I = V / R = 5 / 35 000 ≈ 0.000143 A = 0.143 mA. Remember to multiply by 1000 to convert the current to mA. This current is very small, so it causes no problem even while the button is pressed.

options: Drawing too much current from the pin
The pin not being connected to any voltage, so its reading changes at random
The pin staying LOW all the time
quiz.explanation: On a floating input the pin is connected neither to 5 V nor to GND; noise from the surroundings makes the reading HIGH or LOW at random. That is why INPUT_PULLUP is used. A pin that is always LOW means the pin is connected to GND.
